fix.qnx_fix: Remove the fixed-priority channel attribute so the server channel uses QNX's default client-priority inheritance in all modes. This eliminates the server/client/hog inversion without changing the workload, timing, or CLI semantics; the program still accepts --inherit, but the channel will no longer be reachable in a non-inheriting configuration.
fix.rationale: The live trace shows a classic server-channel priority inversion: the prio-30 client is REPLY-blocked on the prio-10 server, while a prio-20 hog runs and preempts the server. On QNX Neutrino, the correct fix is to let the server channel inherit the highest waiting client priority. The current code conditionally creates a non-inheriting channel via _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY when --inherit is not supplied, which is exactly what enables the inversion. The smallest safe fix is to remove that flag entirely so ChannelCreate() always uses default priority inheritance. This is QNX-correct and works in every mode/flag combination because there is no longer any path that creates a fixed-priority channel.

/* The bug: _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY turns off QNX's client-driven priority inheritance. */
